name: add-your-second-pc
title: Add your second PC
description: Expand your Bluefin Server home cluster by adding a second PC. Choose between joining it as a k3s agent node in the same cluster, or registering a separate cluster as a KubeStellar WEC.
author: Project Bluefin lab
prerequisites: Bluefin Server image booted on the new PC
Network reachability between the new PC and ghost (LAN for shared cluster; reachable hub endpoint for WEC)
kubectl access to the ghost cluster

steps.title: Prerequisites
steps.description: Boot the new PC from the Bluefin Server image. Make sure it can reach ghost. Decide whether this PC should become part of the same k3s cluster (default, one scheduling domain) or remain a separate cluster that joins as a KubeStellar WEC.

steps.title: Choose join mode
steps.description: Shared cluster (default): the PC runs k3s agent and shares the ghost control plane. Live migration is possible and there is no extra control-plane overhead. WEC: the PC is its own cluster, reachable by ghost, and KubeStellar federates workloads to it. Use WEC for remote sites or machines that must stay autonomous.

steps.title: Retrieve the k3s agent token
steps.description: On the server node (ghost), read the k3s agent token. The token is sensitive — copy it but never commit it to git.

steps.title: Install the k3s agent service
steps.description: On the new PC, install k3s agent as a persistent systemd unit. On image-based Bluefin Server systems the binary must go under /var/usrlocal/bin. Replace <server-lan-ip> and <token> with the values from the previous step. The service starts automatically on boot; use `sudo systemctl disable k3s-agent` first if you prefer to opt in manually (see docs/reference/agent-cheatsheet.md).
steps.command: curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | K3S_URL="https://<server-lan-ip>:6443" K3S_TOKEN="<token>" INSTALL_K3S_BIN_DIR="/var/usrlocal/bin" sh -s -

steps.title: Retrieve the hub token (WEC path)
steps.description: If you chose WEC mode, get an OCM bootstrap token from the hub cluster (ghost). This token lets the new cluster register itself.

steps.title: Join as a WEC
steps.description: Run this on the new cluster. Replace <token> with the hub token, <hub-endpoint> with a reachable ghost API address, and <wec-name> with a short name for this cluster. In-LAN clusters can use https://<ghost-lan-ip>:6443; remote clusters need the Gateway API TLSRoute or LoadBalancer endpoint configured per ADR-0004.

steps.title: Accept the WEC
steps.description: Back on the hub cluster, accept the CSR and label the ManagedCluster so lab BindingPolicies can select it by name.
steps.command: clusteradm accept --clusters <wec-name> && kubectl label managedcluster <wec-name> name=<wec-name> --overwrite

steps.title: Verify the join
steps.description: Shared cluster: the new node should appear Ready. WEC: the ManagedCluster should report JOINED and AVAILABLE.
steps.command: kubectl get nodes -o wide && kubectl get managedclusters -o wide

steps.title: Prepare storage for the new node (shared cluster)
steps.description: The local-path provisioner routes PVCs to node-local data disks via the nodePathMap in manifests/local-path-config.yaml. Before scheduling stateful workloads here, open a PR that adds the new node's data-disk path (e.g. /var/mnt/<node>-data/local-path) to that ConfigMap. Never provision storage on root disks. Do not label the node for zot-cache unless you have manually prepared /var/mnt/<node>-data/zot-cache and intend to host the cache there; the existing zot-cache DaemonSet selects on lab.projectbluefin.io/zot-cache-data=true and will fail if the directory is missing.
steps.command: kubectl get configmap local-path-config -n kube-system -o yaml

steps.title: Verify workloads are scheduling on the new node
steps.description: Confirm the scheduler is placing pods on the new capacity. BuildBarn workers and other daemonsets should begin to spread once the node is Ready and any required labels or taints are satisfied.

steps.title: Enjoy the elastic BuildStream grid
steps.description: More nodes mean BuildBarn workers can spread. Run a build pipeline and confirm workers schedule on the new capacity.

troubleshooting.title: Node stays NotReady
troubleshooting.description: Check that the new PC can reach the k3s server on TCP 6443 and that the token is correct. Verify firewall rules allow the agent to reach the server.

troubleshooting.title: ManagedCluster stuck JOINED empty
troubleshooting.description: The CSR may not have been accepted. Re-run accept and ensure the name label is set.
troubleshooting.command: clusteradm accept --clusters <wec-name> && kubectl label managedcluster <wec-name> name=<wec-name> --overwrite
